This file documents licenses for individual js/vendor/ files that don't
carry their own inline license banner. Each section applies only to the
file(s) it names.

================================================================
js/vendor/libheif-bundle.mjs
================================================================

Source:  libheif-js npm package, v1.19.8 (https://www.npmjs.com/package/libheif-js)
         — an Emscripten/WASM build of libheif (https://github.com/strukturag/libheif)
Copied:  package/libheif-wasm/libheif-bundle.mjs from the npm tarball, unmodified,
         to js/vendor/libheif-bundle.mjs — the browser ESM build with the .wasm
         binary embedded inline as base64 (no separate .wasm fetch needed).
License: LGPL-3.0. Full license text: js/vendor/libheif-license/LICENSE-LGPL-3.0.txt
         (copied verbatim from the npm package's libheif-wasm/LICENSE).
Used by: js/heicDecode.js — lazy dynamic `import()`, only loaded the first
         time a user actually selects a .heic/.heif file in the jpg2pdf
         tool. Decodes entirely client-side (WASM in the browser); no file
         or pixel data is ever sent to a server. Loaded and used as-is,
         not modified or relinked into another binary — LGPL-3.0 §4/§5
         "aggregation"/"combined work" terms are satisfied by this exact
         usage (dynamically loaded, unmodified, source available at the
         URL above).

================================================================
js/vendor/qpdf/worker.js, js/vendor/qpdf/lib/qpdf.js, js/vendor/qpdf/lib/qpdf.wasm
================================================================

Source:  qpdf-run npm package, v0.2.1 (https://www.npmjs.com/package/qpdf-run)
         — an Emscripten/WASM build of qpdf (https://github.com/qpdf/qpdf).
         Bundled qpdf core: 11.7.0 (confirmed via the version string embedded
         directly in qpdf.wasm, not assumed from the wrapper's own version).
Copied:  Origin tarball qpdf-run-0.2.1.tgz sits at the repo root; added in
         commit 7b4b09d9 ("Phase 2"). See js/vendor/SOURCE.txt for full
         provenance/usage notes and a known-CVE tracking entry.
License: Two licenses apply, since this bundles two separate works:
         - qpdf-run (the wrapper/build tooling itself): MIT.
         - qpdf (the compiled code making up the bulk of qpdf.wasm): Apache
           License 2.0 — confirmed via the license text compiled directly
           into the binary's own `--copyright` CLI output strings. qpdf
           offers Artistic License 2.0 as an alternative at the licensee's
           option, per that same embedded text ("you may continue to
           consider qpdf to be licensed under those terms").
Used by: js/decryptPdf.js (owner-only decrypt preflight on every uploaded
         PDF, via js/files.js) and the Unlock PDF tool (js/processor.js's
         _runUnlock). Runs entirely client-side inside a Web Worker; no
         file is ever sent to a server. Loaded and used as-is, not modified.

================================================================
js/vendor/sRGB2014.icc
================================================================

Copyright, as embedded directly in the profile's own 'cprt' tag
(extracted and verified from the binary before this file was written):

    Copyright International Color Consortium, 2015

'desc' tag: sRGB2014

Source: https://www.color.org — the ICC's own reference sRGB profile,
published for use as an embeddable, redistributable color profile in
color-managed documents and images. This is the profile's stated
purpose: ICC reference profiles are designed to be embedded in
third-party files (PDFs, images) by any color-managed software,
which is exactly this project's use case (embedding as the
/DestOutputProfile stream in a PDF/A /OutputIntents entry).

Note: this session had no working internet access to re-fetch and
re-read color.org's current outward-facing terms-of-use page directly;
the copyright line above was extracted straight from the binary itself
(byte offset 2924, tag 'cprt') as the most authoritative fact available
here, cross-checked against the file's ICC header ('acsp' signature,
'mntr RGB XYZ' profile class) to confirm it's a genuine, unmodified
ICC Consortium profile and not a relabeled or corrupted file. If this
profile is ever relied on for a legally-sensitive PDF/A archiving
claim, re-verify current terms at color.org before shipping.
